approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a population of scored molecular graphs and fits a count-fingerprint Gaussian process only to the current session's accepted observations. For each purchase it builds a fresh field through a persistent sampled function: four-member beams guide eight waves of graph edits on top of the common offspring pool. After every path is complete, a stall-dependent screen keeps the forty highest real GP means when active. A separate independent joint posterior draw then chooses each purchase within that frozen screen, excluding identities already bought. Actual oracle feedback updates the archive, greedy survivors and subsequent breeding.
approach.novelty: Remove the sampled residual only from that final independent purchase decision: buy the highest available real GP mean on each completed field, while the stochastic guide continues to construct the field and every independent judge draw is retained passively. The measured judge orders paid outcomes worse than the real mean, which motivates testing whether its extra selection noise obstructs useful root improvement after random exploration has already occurred. There are no listed same-Parent siblings. Earlier mean-only controls acted on fresh offspring fields; this experiment leaves coherent stochastic graph exploration intact and measures this final consumer's conditional contribution.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior of the actual code Parent n-b5d3c2aee387 is poor conversion of correctly sampled independent final-judge maxima into full-session positive scored-root gain. Its complete Search panel has mean endpoint 0.5290667545232163, population SD 0.0658767199241255, seed means 0.569040310023852/0.436202000076089/0.581957953469708, and a paired -0.04896320625023165 against its own Parent n-dc60d82e4f36. All three supplied summary.json and run.log pairs report complete successful execution. Its registered full root gain falls from 0.0035516224072537706 to 0.0027959508608351906 per purchase on every seed mean; this remains refuted/triggered, never a technical recovery. All 4350 judges reconstruct and 4117 paid choices differ from the passive guide, so exposure was present. The judge correctly orders 9357/19456 untied co-purchased pairs, versus 13693/19456 for the real GP mean, yet still overpredicts 4011 outcomes and 3699 purchases do not beat their real roots. Base purchases rise from 954 to 2849 and mean extension depth falls from 1.78 to 0.57. The improvement in late root gain to 0.0021704829207712284, greater root-beater count and lower selected optimism do not rescue the full prediction. These are observed-stream diagnostics, not rewards for unpurchased alternatives or a demonstrated mediator. Sources: nodes/n-b5d3c2aee387/analysis.json, nodes/n-b5d3c2aee387/molecular.json, nodes/n-dc60d82e4f36/analysis.json, policy/responses/curate-67ac875e8c83.json and policy/scratch/search_policy-74d2dea100a9/evidence-review.json. Strong contrary residual-removal results remain: n-c4c934fd6a68 loses 0.12689408391255833 on its fresh-field masked host; n-2d61abf0b2bd and n-7d9afd9af925 lose 0.018621410181405656 and 0.09438631107688404 for restricted-only and unrestricted-only fresh-field removals. Their canonical analysis.json files retain positive conditional residual contributions. n-eb15da16dbea establishes executed coherent construction but refuted useful-transfer prediction; n-dc60d82e4f36 confirms the later final screen. Only those implemented capabilities are inherited.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse the ticket's frozen review after reading its observed bottleneck, actual recorded discovery queries, primary-source findings and applicability, and exact position-2 internal-evidence adoption record. This PLAN made no new literature search and borrows no new external recipe, so queries/sources/adoptions here are empty; the inherited queries and sources remain in the referenced review. The B1 observed bottleneck and B3 changed-consumer/counterexample review support one testable removal, not literature authority or continuation of the refuted prediction. Exact Parent implementation and bounded receipt feasibility support implementation within the frozen scope; efficacy and conditional component sign remain open.
literature_review.internal_evidence_reason: The frozen review and its position-2 record in policy/scratch/search_policy-74d2dea100a9/literature-adoptions.json explicitly choose internal evidence: complete independent-judge exposure, worse same-paid ordering than the already computed real GP mean, and a full-gain refutation motivate pricing this final consumer while preserving stochastic exploration. Historical opposite removal signs are retained. No paper supplies a claim that mean-only final judging must help, and no new model or package is introduced.

hypothesis: Remove m-000000000006 sampled residual influence solely at the successful final independent-judge purchase consumer on n-b5d3c2aee387. For each completed path j, let F_j be its unchanged graph field, E_j its original frozen K3/M40 real-mean eligibility set (the whole field when unrestricted), and U_j the actual previously seen or already selected identities. After every original judge has been drawn and checked, choose the first identity in the existing canonical-tie mean_ranking that belongs to E_j and is absent from U_j: equivalently argmax over F_j intersect E_j minus U_j of its exact real-data GP mean. Update only the actual sequential unavailable set with that choice. The guide's latent residual remains active throughout graph construction; the independent judge residual remains computed with full within-field covariance and original numerical/random law but has zero influence on successful purchases. The testable path is final-consumer removal -> changed actual choices toward exact existing means on stochastically explored fields -> potentially higher complete equal-session positive scored-root gain and endpoint performance. This is a conditional residual-presence removal, not a retuned guide/judge dependence hypothesis, covariance/correlation removal, mask removal, intermediate mean screen or new predictor.

finding_summary.headline: Mean-only final judging raised root gain and score while concentrating purchases in fewer cores
finding_summary.insights:
This confirms the registered mean-judge useful-transfer prediction and supports negative retained endpoint contribution of the final independent residual consumer on this finite matched panel. It does not rehabilitate the Parent's refuted independent-judging prediction or reverse the positive residual contributions measured on fresh-pool hosts. Preserved common-input fields and complete draw/choice reconstruction rule out absent exposure or an altered guide as explanations. The original mean mask remained constructed but was nonbinding for every mean-selected purchase, so this removal does not independently price that mask or its interaction with the residual. No new literature recipe was adopted; the intervention was explicitly based on internal evidence.

Useful root improvements and a favorable panel mean coexist with substantial endpoint losses. The aggregate endpoint gain depends on a large docking recovery in one seed, with eleven other endpoint cells adverse. On the Child's actual paid products, the mean orders 62.6% of untied co-purchased outcomes correctly, versus 55.8% for the passive judge and 55.1% for the guide. The Parent mean ordered 70.4% correctly on its different purchased population. Lower mean prediction error therefore does not establish uniformly better ranking, and neither these comparisons nor passive alternatives identify a mediator or an alternative endpoint.

The search concentrates more strongly into local analog families. Base-field purchases increase from 2,849 to 2,992 and mean paid extension depth falls from 0.57 to 0.36 despite retaining all eight expansion waves. Typed/generic nonempty scaffold counts fall from 2,016/1,245 to 710/239, and fragment-excluded nearest-neighbor similarity rises in every task. Fewer extension purchases nevertheless produce more measured positive root gain per purchase, from 0.003124 to 0.007629; this is selected-stream evidence, not the value of the unbought extensions. Most purchases still fail to beat their roots (3,563), and 2,911 nonterminal products never become roots of later accepted purchases. A search scheme that preserves access to several supported cores, or a ranking model aimed at useful improvements, could address that concentration; its benefit remains untested. The Molecular report also narrows the chemistry limitation: both size tails contract, from 103 to four tiny products and 428 to 311 large products, while nitrogen-halogen and peroxide connections increase and explicit stereochemistry remains absent. Context-preserving proposal operators could address those attachment and core-access gaps, but these associations do not justify a universal size cutoff, chemistry reward or approach-level verdict.
finding_summary.results:
The final mean rule ran correctly for all 4,350 purchases across fifteen Search sessions and changed 3,909 choices relative to the passive independent judge on the same available fields. All original stochastic guides and judge computations were preserved. All paid labels reached feedback, with 4,200 next-fit confirmations and 150 terminal censors.

Full positive gain over the original scored generating roots rose from 0.00279595 to 0.00413786 per purchase, an increase of 0.00134191. It increased on all three seed averages and in nine of fifteen task/seed sessions; six sessions declined. Root-beating purchases rose from 651 to 787, and total positive root gain from 12.16239 to 17.99970. The registered useful-transfer falsifier did not trigger. Late gain rose slightly, from 0.00217048 to 0.00234774, while falling in twelve of the fifteen late-session comparisons.

Final mean score increased from 0.529067 to 0.545027, a paired gain of 0.015961, above the descriptive 0.002 scale. Four task/seed endpoints improved and eleven declined. Seed macro differences were -0.022410, +0.127741 and -0.057450; the largest gain was +0.708396 in docking seed 1. Macro population SD across these three seeds fell from 0.065877 to 0.016139. The code-Parent task-regression check passes, while the separate formal Anchor comparison is -0.062003 and flags docking and sitagliptin. These are protocol comparisons, not reliability estimates. All independent judges remained computed, costing about 20.1 seconds per session, mostly receipt logging.

molecular.headline: Aromatic cores persist with far fewer scaffolds; tiny fragments recede, but N-halogen bonds and undefined stereochemistry remain
molecular.overall_character: The frozen context separately reports complete Child evaluation and complete pairing with actual code Parent n-b5d3c2aee387. All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent Search trajectories were read in full; no paired path or task is missing. Each node contributes 4,350 accepted optimizer products, with the 150 initial observations retained separately. These are purchased outputs; the trajectories do not enumerate every internally considered graph. The Child produces substituted indoles and aryl carboxamides, aminoallenes, nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino heterocycles, linked heteroaromatic frameworks, halogenated aminoalkyl compounds and connected cyclic amides. The digest ring-marker and aromatic-marker rates are each 0.9954 to 1.0. These are fractions of strings containing markers, not aromatic-atom fractions or perceived ring counts. RDKit finds rings in 4,346 products and aromatic atoms in 4,345. Median size is 32 heavy atoms versus Parent 29. Both size tails contract: four products have at most six heavy atoms versus 103, and 311 have at least fifty versus 428; maxima are 68 versus 120. This does not settle chemistry quality: nitrogen-halogen bonds occur in 1,479 products versus 877, oxygen-halogen bonds in 63 versus 756, and oxygen-oxygen bonds in 172 versus 81. Ordinary amine connectivity is present in 1,552 products, including 708 ring-amine matches, versus Parent 2,019 and 926; neutral SMILES do not imply absent ionizability. There are 710 typed and 239 generic nonempty Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 2,016 and 1,245. Several distinct core families remain, but every task has fewer scaffolds and higher within-task nearest-neighbor similarity after excluding products with at most six heavy atoms. This supports a reading of concentrated analog series rather than missing ring-generation capability. Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 2,375 products versus 2,976; neither node has assigned centres. Potential unspecified double-bond stereo occurs in 1,403 versus 1,290 products, with zero specified cases for both. These toolkit exposures do not enumerate stable stereoisomers. Small perceived rings whose atoms are all aromatic occur in 286 products versus 177; the flag is a geometry-review cue, not proof of an impossible structure. No synthetic route, conformer, stability measurement, pKa or stereoisomer comparison is provided. The drug-likeness chip describes structural familiarity only. All early/late purchases, both size tails and lower/upper score deciles are retained. Deciles contain 29 products per session or 87 per pooled task; pooled bands can reflect different seed histories and are descriptive associations. Similarity uses nonchiral 2048-bit radius-two Morgan fingerprints, excludes the same row only, and retains shared identities across seeds. Carbonyl/amide SMARTS with uppercase carbon exclude aromatic lactams; the generic cumulated-double query also matches sulfonyl groups and is not an allene count. Approximate ring-finding warnings are retained in policy/scratch/r0079-01-improve-L01/molecular/audit.log. Parent definitions from nodes/n-b5d3c2aee387/molecular.json were retained, and recomputation exactly reproduces its archived full, early, late, tail and score-band summaries. Methods, sources and hashes: policy/scratch/r0079-01-improve-L01/molecular/evidence-manifest.json; derived data: policy/scratch/r0079-01-improve-L01/molecular/descriptor-summary.json.

per_task.generated_character: Most products retain a compact indole-like fused heteroarene and a phenyl or pyridyl substituent, with methoxy, alkyl and halomethyl decoration. Median size is 25 heavy atoms and three rings, matching the Parent. Seed 0 develops an aminoallene linking the fused aromatic core to a pyridyl group, including nitrogen-bound fluorine, chlorine or bromine. Seed 1 retains indole carboxamides with vinyl/alkoxy substituents; seed 2 favors related hydrazide-like linkers, including nitrogen-fluorinated variants. The ordinary aromatic and amide fragments are recognizable synthetic motifs, but the complete N-halogenated cumulene and hydrazide combinations have no route evidence. Typed/generic scaffold counts are 78/21 versus Parent 240/101; fragment-excluded mean nearest-neighbor similarity is 0.828 versus 0.733. Only four tiny products remain versus Parent 24, and neither node has a product with at least fifty heavy atoms. liabilities: N-halogen bonds increase to 305 products from Parent 128, and the leading aminoallenes combine unusual nitrogen attachment with cumulated unsaturation. These are local synthesis and reactivity review issues, not measured instability.
The four tiny products all occur late and in weak-score regions. Many other weak products remain ring-rich, so preserving a ring alone is insufficient.
missing_features: The weakest contracted products lack the intact connected aromatic arrangement of the upper families; ring construction itself is already well represented.

The upper band occupies only two generic cores versus Parent eight. Equally supported alternatives with more ordinary nitrogen substitution are sparsely demonstrated; the observations identify no unique missing target scaffold.
Explicit configuration is absent in the 36 products with perceived tetrahedral centres. The data do not establish a preferred configuration or its effect on score.

Ring or halogen presence alone therefore does not reproduce the supported compact arrangement. The final seed-2 hydrazide scores 0.2839873032924116.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
